articles.title: Finland warns Ukraine war ‘spilling over’ after Baltic Sea drone strike on Russian cargo ship
articles.summary: A Russian cargo ship with links to the military was hit by drones and caught fire in the Baltic Sea on Saturday in what Finland said was likely an attack by Ukraine, and the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters.
articles.body: A Russian cargo ship with links to the military was hit by drones and caught fire in the Baltic Sea on Saturday in what Finland said was likely an attack by Ukraine, and the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters. The 16-member crew of the Sparta II evacuated onto lifeboats, then to a nearby Russian ship, and is on its way back to Russia, Finnish Border Guard Commander Ilja Iljin told public broadcaster Yle late on Saturday. Ukraine has sent waves of military drones towards Russia’s northwest Leningrad region this year, including some that strayed into the airspace of the Baltic region, leading to fears that the war was affecting NATO territory. “It is likely that Ukraine … is behind (the attack),” Finnish armed forces spokesperson Aki-Mauri Huhtinen told a press conference, adding it was not clear why the vessel had been targeted. The ship, bound for Russian exclave Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters west of Russia’s Gogland island, Finland’s Defence Forces said, corroborating an earlier account by Russian officials. The blaze was ongoing late on Saturday and Finland is leading the rescue operation as the ship is at anchor in its waters, although Russian vessels may eventually tow the wreckage home, Finnish authorities said. A Russian helicopter was suspected of briefly violating Finnish airspace during the rescue operation, said Mikko Simola, commander of the Gulf of Finland Coast Guard. ‘War is spilling over’ Helsinki said it had introduced temporary aviation and maritime restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland to protect civilians and allow authorities to operate if drones needed to be intercepted. “The war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas. Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor,” Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said on X. Swedish combat aircraft, operating under Finnish command, took part in safeguarding Finland’s and NATO’s territorial integrity following the incident, Sweden’s Defence Minister Pal Jonson said. Finland and Sweden are NATO’s newest member states, joining the military alliance in 2023 and 2024, respectively, in response to Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. “The consequences of fighting Russia’s aggression have reached the Baltic Sea. Another signal for the aggressor to stop. But nothing will stop us from supporting Ukraine,” Estonia’s Prime Minister Kristen Michal wrote on X. Estonia sent a navy vessel to assist in the rescue operation, including firefighting and pollution response, its government said. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Russia’s embassy in Helsinki did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The vessel is subject to US sanctions and is linked to Russian shipping company Oboronlogistika, according to the US Treasury Department. Oboronlogistika provides logistics services for the Russian Defence Ministry, according to the company’s website. “At the moment, there is no confirmed information about what cargo is on board, but it cannot be ruled out that there is military materiel on board,” Iljin of the Finnish Border Guard said. Russia says drones shot down over Leningrad region Leningrad region Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said on Telegram that a cargo vessel had been attacked by two drones in international waters about 3 nautical miles from Russia’s border. Drozdenko also said 80 drones had been shot down over the Leningrad region overnight. Finland’s military said last week it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area during a wave of Ukrainian drone attacks on the Leningrad region. Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said the incident posed no threat to supplies to the region. Kaliningrad, which lies between Poland and Lithuania, has periodically been a flashpoint between Russia and NATO and the European Union. Russia has previously described attacks on its commercial vessels outside its territorial waters as acts of terrorism and maritime piracy. The Sparta II is a 121-metre (397-foot) Russian-flagged cargo vessel owned by Oboronlogistika that left St Petersburg on Friday, according to LSEG data. The Gulf of Finland is a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea between Finland and Estonia that extends east to St Petersburg. Gogland lies in the eastern Gulf of Finland.

articles.title: An Ohio landlord mistakenly removed a tenant's belongings, including paintings and ceramics made by her sister; though she had no receipts or photographs, an appeals court upheld her $6,000 award
articles.summary: An Ohio woman has won a $6,000 court award after her landlord mistakenly removed her belongings from her apartment, including paintings and ceramic pieces
articles.body: An Ohio woman has won a $6,000 court award after her landlord mistakenly removed her belongings from her apartment, including paintings and ceramic pieces made by her sister. Although she had no receipts or photographs of the missing items, an appeals court ruled that her testimony and research into their value were sufficient to support the compensation.The Ohio Court of Appeals, Eighth District, upheld the award on November 19 in a case involving tenant Grace Davis and Alpha Apartment Management LLC. According to the court's judgment, there was no dispute that the property manager's staff had mistakenly entered Davis's apartment and removed her personal belongings.According to Law Justia, Davis prepared an itemised list of the missing possessions and estimated the value of each. Her total claim was $6,633. After the management company offered her a lower amount, she filed a small-claims case to recover the loss.How the landlord removed her belongings by mistakeDuring the small-claims trial on February 17, 2026, Davis explained how she calculated the value of the items. She said she searched online to find out how much it would cost to replace them. Some of the belongings were gifts, including paintings and ceramic pieces made by her sister. For those items, Davis asked her sister how much it would cost to make them again."I just looked up how much it would cost to replace the items," Davis told the court, according to the judgment. She also explained that she had asked her sister about the cost of recreating the handmade pieces. Davis acknowledged that she did not have receipts or photographs of the belongings. Some had been in her possession for years, while others had been given to her as gifts.A maintenance worker employed by Alpha confirmed that he had removed bags and bins from the apartment. The property manager also admitted that the belongings had been removed by mistake. However, she questioned Davis's claim, saying she could not simply pay her $6,000 without proof or photographs. Davis maintained that the figures on her list were based on research through the internet and other sources.Court accepts her valuation despite missing receiptsOn March 3, 2026, a magistrate ruled in Davis's favour. The magistrate found that she had explained how she valued the belongings and that her assessment had been made with reasonable care. Although Davis had claimed $6,633, the magistrate awarded her $6,000, the maximum amount permitted in the small-claims court, along with interest and costs.Alpha challenged the decision, arguing that Davis had relied on replacement costs rather than the market value of the belongings. The company also argued that she should receive only nominal damages, which it said should not exceed $500.On April 20, 2026, the trial court rejected the company's objection. It noted that several items on Davis's list, including custom ceramic pieces from family, framed artwork from family and estate sales, and framed family photographs, could not be valued simply by checking the price of a similar product in a shop.The court found that Davis had made a reasonable effort to establish the value of her lost possessions rather than offering guesses or unsupported estimates.Appeals court rejects landlord's challengeAlpha then took the matter to the Ohio Court of Appeals, Eighth District, arguing that the $6,000 award was not supported by the correct method of calculating property damages. However, the appeals court found no reason to overturn the decision.In its November 19 ruling, the court explained that although market value is generally used to calculate compensation for damaged or wrongfully taken personal property, that standard is not always practical for unique or difficult-to-replace belongings.The judgment also referred to earlier Ohio Supreme Court decisions recognising that owners can testify about the value of their own property. It noted that small-claims proceedings allow more flexibility in assessing evidence and that estimates can be used, provided the claimed loss is established with reasonable certainty rather than speculation.The appeals court also pointed out that Alpha had the opportunity to question Davis about her list and valuations but did not provide an alternative estimate for the missing items.The judges concluded that the trial court had applied the appropriate legal standard and that its findings were supported by the evidence. The court therefore affirmed the $6,000 award and ordered that Davis recover the costs of the appeal.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Bahrain says Iranian attack causes fire at industrial facility
articles.summary: Bahrain reports no injuries, as Iran’s IRGC says it targeted US military positions at two bases in al-Riffa and Awali.
articles.body:
Bahrain says an Iranian attack has struck a civilian industrial facility, starting a fire, in the latest escalation of the war in the Middle East.

Bahrain’s Defence Force said its air defences intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks late on Saturday.

In a post on X, Bahrain’s Ministry of Interior said the attack was part of “Iranian aggression”.

It said preliminary reports pointed to material damage but no injuries, and that civil defence teams were working to bring the fire under control.

The Interior Ministry did not name the facility or say where it was. Earlier, air raid sirens sounded in Bahrain, and the ministry urged residents to move to the nearest safe place without saying what the threat was.

In a statement after the attack, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it had carried out a combined missile and drone operation targeting United States military positions at the al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain.

The IRGC claimed it destroyed two US Patriot air defence radars at the bases.

The attack was “in response to continued aggression and violations of the airspace of the Islamic Republic of Iran”, the statement said.

“After two US MQ-1 and MQ-9 reconnaissance and combat drones violated Iranian airspace, US military positions at the aforementioned bases were targeted in an operation by the IRGC Aerospace Force,” it added.

Earlier, Iran’s semi-official Fars news agency reported that the IRGC had attacked two military bases used by US forces at Sheikh Isa and Juffair.

The IRGC said that operation, as well as being in response to continued violations of Iranian airspace, came following a US attack on a radar installation on Iran’s Hengam Island.

Iran’s state news agency IRNA reported that an interceptor missile launched from the US Fifth Fleet base in Bahrain had also crashed on Sitra Island and started a large fire. It cited an outlet called Bahrain News, which blamed a recurring malfunction in the Patriot air defence system.

Bahrain hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet. It has been attacked repeatedly since the US-Israel war on Iran began in late February, including three drone attacks in recent days after a lull of several weeks.

Other Gulf states have also come under repeated fire from Tehran since the US-Israel war began.

In a statement on X, Bahrain’s Foreign Ministry called on the United Nations Security Council to take “firm measures to compel Iran” to implement Resolution 2817.

The resolution, adopted on March 11, condemns Iranian attacks against Gulf states and Jordan, and demands an immediate halt to hostilities and maritime interference.

The head of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) expressed his “full solidarity” with Bahrain following Iran’s attack on the industrial facility.

Jassim Mohamed AlBudaiwi, GCC secretary-general, said Bahrain’s security, territorial integrity, facilities, citizens and residents are an integral part of the security of the GCC states, and that the council stands united in confronting threats to their security and stability.

The GCC backs “all measures” Bahrain takes to deal with the attack, he added.

articles.title: China's support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor impacted Indian planning: US panel
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A US commission has claimed that China's backing of Pakistan during Operation Sindoor had complicated Indian operational planning and tied down
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A US commission has claimed that China's backing of Pakistan during Operation Sindoor had complicated Indian operational planning and tied down Indian military resources, advancing China's goal of constraining and suppressing India's rise as a peer competitor in the Indo-Pacific region."India is one of the few powers outside the US alliance system with the scale to materially affect the long-term competition with China. China understands this, and it is actively working to suppress India's rise across multiple domains," said the latest annual report by US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC). USCC is an independent govt agency created by Congress in 2000 to monitor, probe and submit annual reports on national security and economic implications of bilateral trade and defence ties between US and China. According to the report, China's evolving military partnership with Pakistan has made a two-front contingency an increasingly critical concern for India. "May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict demonstrated how China could strengthen Pakistan during a crisis without Beijing entering the fighting directly, adding to India's concerns about how a future conflict with Pakistan could develop," it said.The USCC report said India’s dependence on Chinese manufacturing has become a key source of leverage for Beijing — and a growing vulnerability for the US.“China has restricted industrial inputs, equipment, technology and expertise to India and required some Indian firms to certify that Chinesesupplied goods would not be reexported to the US. Chinese pricing has also undercut new Indian pharmaceutical production, illustrating Beijing’s intent to undermine Indian suppliers that can compete with established Chinese producers,” it said, adding these dependencies complicate US efforts to diversify supply chains away from China by shifting production to India.It said China’s expanding naval and surveillance presence is beginning to erode India’s longstanding strategic advantages in the Indian Ocean and place additional demands on Indian forces. It said China is beginning to bring its South China Sea playbook to the Indian Ocean, renaming undersea features in ways that could lay the groundwork for potential claims of jurisdiction.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Over 10k postgraduate medical seats in blocked category; govt may review float system
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: More than 10,000 postgraduate medical seats were listed under the blocked category after Round 2 of NEET-PG 2026 counselling, with the data
articles.body: NEW DELHI: More than 10,000 postgraduate medical seats were listed under the blocked category after Round 2 of NEET-PG 2026 counselling, with the data indicating that some candidates were holding one seat through All India counselling and another through state counselling simultaneously, prompting the govt to consider changes to the newly introduced float system.According to the SARTHA app, a medical admission and counselling platform for NEET-PG and NEET-UG aspirants, 10,105 seats were listed under the 'Blocking' category after Round 2 of NEET-PG 2026 counselling. The app, filtered for MCC (All India) counselling, describes these as seats held by students who also have an allotment in another counselling process. The data was shared by Dr Kapil Dev on social media.The branch-wise breakup showed MD General Medicine accounting for the highest number of blocked seats at 1,026, followed by MS Obstetrics and Gynaecology (861) and MS General Surgery (786), according to the app. Dr Nachiket Bhatia, a medico-socio activist, has also flagged the issue on his social media account.A senior official familiar with the counselling process said the float facility, which allows candidates to retain an allotted seat while seeking an upgrade, could be contributing to dual seat blocking as all-India and state counselling run parallelly on separate platforms. "A candidate may opt for float in both processes and end up blocking two seats," the official said.Introduced for students' convenience, the facility allows candidates to retain seats while seeking an upgrade, with physical joining becoming compulsory in the third round. The official said govt may consider restricting float to the first round and making physical joining compulsory from the second round in future counselling cycles. "This is the first time we have introduced the float system in this manner. We will analyse the situation after the third round."The official also flagged the absence of a common counselling platform linking all-India and state processes, which run simultaneously on separate portals, making it difficult to track candidates holding seats in both. A common portal could prevent multiple allotments, but differences in state reservation policies and concerns over loss of control have hindered integration.Meanwhile, Federation of All India Medical Association has sought a 24-hour deferment of NEET-PG Round 2 results and a one-day window for eligible candidates to surrender either their All India or state quota seats.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: Utah vs. TCU betting preview: Why TCU +7.5, the Horned Frogs moneyline and the under 46.5 are the plays for Saturday night in Fort Worth.
articles.body: Utah has done everything right this season. The Utes are 10-0, No. 2 in the College Football Playoff rankings and riding a 16-game winning streak dating to last season. They're in line for a first-round bye, and in Morgan Scalley's first year, they're the best story in the Big 12. That's also why Saturday night in Fort Worth is a dangerous spot for the Utes. Over the last two weeks, Utah has played two games that would drain any team. It beat rival BYU 28-20 in the Holy War, then had to rally for a 40-39 win at Arizona which was a bit of a letdown spot in its own right. Now the Utes are on the road again, for a 9:00 p.m. ET kickoff against a TCU team fighting for bowl eligibility, with one of the best defenses in the country, in what will surely be a rowdy atmosphere. FIVE COLLEGE FOOTBALL BETS FOR SATURDAY, INCLUDING TWO ROAD DOGS THAT ARE BEING SLEPT ON The market sees an unbeaten team against a .500 team. I see a letdown spot, a defense built to slow Utah down and a lot of bad luck about to turn around. Utah -265 | TCU +215Spread: Utah -7.5 (-105) | TCU +7.5 (-115)Total: 46.5 (Over -110 / Under -110) Saturday, Nov. 21, 9 p.m. ET, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth, FOX The public is all-in on Utah This is about as lopsided as a betting market gets. Between 82% and 90% of the spread tickets are on Utah, and the Utes have drawn between 73% and 84% of the money. The line has moved around with that action. Utah opened at -6.5, climbed as high as -7.5 and has settled between -7 and -7.5 depending on the book. The public is backing the undefeated team with the shiny ranking, and the books are happy to take it. I love a classic contrarian spot, and in this one, I'm happy to go the other way. WHAT IS A TEASER BET? HOW TEASERS WORK IN FOOTBALL AND BASKETBALL BETTING The letdown spot is real Spots like this are where unbeaten teams lose. Utah has been in close games almost every week since late September, and the last two were especially challenging. Winning a rivalry game against BYU and then rallying on the road at Arizona takes a lot out of a roster. This is the third straight week the Utes have played a meaningful, high-stress game, and it's another road trip with a late kickoff. Don't get me wrong, I fully understand that Utah's offense is still dangerous. Devon Dampier has accounted for 31 touchdowns, 22 passing and nine rushing, and the Utes are scoring 37.9 points per game, 15th in the country. But this is the kind of game where good teams can look flat for a half, and against this defense, a flat half can be enough to put the Utes in trouble. ESPN DISMISSES UTAH UTES AS NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP CONTENDERS DESPITE BIG WIN OVER BYU: 'THEY WON'T WIN' TCU's defense is the equalizer Utah's offense isn't the only elite unit in this one. TCU's record hides how good its defense has been. The Horned Frogs allow just 15.2 points per game, 12th in the country, and they rank ninth nationally in net adjusted EPA per play allowed. That's the matchup that matters. TCU has been at its best against offenses like Utah's. Under Sonny Dykes, the Horned Frogs are 17-7 straight up and 15-8-1 against the spread against teams averaging at least 425 yards per game. Dykes is also 6-3 against the spread as an underdog of 3.5 to 10 points, right in the range of this line. TCU is due some luck This is the stat that makes the case, and I promise it's not a stretch. TCU has lost five games this season, and all five were decided by one score. Against Power 4 opponents, the Horned Frogs are 1-5 in one-score games, the most such losses of any Power 4 team. They've battled, but things have consistently gone against the Horned Frogs in close ones. On the other side, Utah is 4-0 in those games. One could make the argument that good teams find a way to win those games, and that's true. But it's also true that there is some inherent luck in close games, and expecting that to always go your way i playing with fire. Close-game records rarely hold over a full season. TCU hasn't been five losses worse than its opponents. It's been a handful of plays worse. Utah hasn't been four wins better, either. Eventually those coin flips start landing the other way, and a home game against a conference opponent with national championship aspirations is a good place for that to start for TCU. WHAT IS A MONEYLINE BET? — HOW MONEYLINE ODDS, PAYOUTS AND FAVORITES WORK The case for Utah It's only fair to make Utah's case too. The Utes are 8-2 against the spread and 7-1 as favorites of 6.5 or more. They score at an elite rate, and their defense allows only 18.6 points per game, 21st in the country. TCU's offense is the real concern. The Horned Frogs score just 23.4 points per game, 103rd nationally, and they've been inconsistent all season. If Jaden Craig, who has thrown one interception over the last three games, can't move the ball, TCU's defense will eventually wear down. That's why the points matter. I don't need TCU to outscore Utah. I need its defense to keep this within a score. If you're not a true believer in TCU at home, take the points. TCU +7.5 (-115) This is the main play. Utah is in a letdown spot, the public is lopsided and TCU's defense is good enough to keep this close. The Horned Frogs have lost five games by a combined handful of plays. Getting more than a touchdown at home with that profile is the best number on the board. TCU moneyline (+215) If you believe in the letdown, take a smaller piece of the upset. At +215, the moneyline implies TCU wins about 32% of the time. With a top-12 scoring defense at home against a tired team on the road, that feels low. Under 46.5 (-110) The total fits the same story. TCU games have gone over just twice in 10 tries, and the Horned Frogs have averaged only 18.3 points per game in conference play. The early under action has been heavy, with every tracked ticket and dollar on the total backing the under. If TCU's defense keeps Utah out of rhythm and its own offense grinds, this lands in the low 40s. That's the type of game where the underdog covers. The bottom line Utah is a great team, and it may still be a great futures bet to win the national title. But a 10-0 team playing its third straight high-stress game, on the road, late at night, against a top-12 defense with nothing to lose is how upsets happen. articles.title: Lebanese president demands Israel withdrawal, decries Iran’s interference
articles.summary: Joseph Aoun says ‘two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked’ mean Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence.
articles.body:
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has decried Iran’s meddling in Lebanon’s affairs and demanded Israel’s withdrawal from his country’s south.

In a speech on Saturday, on the eve of Lebanon’s 83rd independence anniversary, Aoun said Lebanon faces two interconnected fateful tests: the “Israeli occupation of parts of our land” and “foreign interference” from “some influential parties in the Iranian regime” through weapons and decisions outside the authority of the Lebanese state.

These “two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked” mean that Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence, he added.

“Withdraw from every inch of Lebanese territory. Stop your attacks. And return our captives,” Aoun demanded of Israel.

Dozens of Lebanese citizens are believed to be held in Israeli detention centres , including civilians as well as members of the Hezbollah armed group captured during fighting in southern Lebanon.

The president also pledged to press ahead with plans to bring all weapons under state control, declaring that there would be “no weapons outside the state that take orders from, or serve the interests of foreign powers.”

“You must hand over your weapons,” Aoun said.

Lebanon’s government has promised to disarm Hezbollah, the Iran-backed Lebanese group whose arsenal has long outstripped that of the national army and that has justified its weapons as necessary to resist Israel.

Lebanon and Israel signed a framework agreement in June, following US-mediated talks, which included the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanese territories and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the area.

But implementation has stalled, with Hezbollah refusing to surrender its weapons and Israel continuing to strike Lebanon.

On Saturday, Israeli strikes hit the districts of Nabatieh, Bint Jbeil and Marjayoun in southern Lebanon.

Al Jazeera correspondents reported that one of the air strikes hit the outskirts of Baraachit, a town in Bint Jbeil.

They said Baraachit came under Israeli gunfire at dawn and reported the movement of Israeli military vehicles on the outskirts of the town.

The NNA reported that Israeli forces carried out three explosions in Wadi al-Khiam in the Marjayoun district, but gave no further details.

Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon have killed at least 4,386 people and wounded 12,407 others since March 2, when the latest Hezbollah-Israel war started.

articles.title: I Am Helen: Nicola Coughlan on her uncomfortable new TV drama
articles.summary: I Am Helen is a must-watch according to critics, but the cast don't want viewers sitting comfortably.
articles.body:
If you want to unwind on the sofa after a long day, I Am Helen probably isn't the show for you.

The Channel 4 drama starring Bridgerton star Nicola Coughlan and Joe Cole from Peaky Blinders has been called a must-watch by critics - but the cast don't want viewers sitting comfortably.

"There's going to be a few awkward sofas," Cole, who plays Helen's partner Steve, says.

"There's going to be people up and down the country that will be able to relate to this in varying degrees.

"And if we can put that in their living rooms and open up a debate, open up a conversation - and maybe help people be better - then we've done our job."

I Am Helen is the latest project in director Dominic Savage's I Am... series, female-led stories focusing on themes like mental health and relationships.

The two fully-improvised episodes, devised in collaboration with Coughlan, follow a relationship spiralling after Steve tries to choke Helen during sex without consent.

"We never realised how incredibly timely it would be," Coughlan tells BBC Newsbeat.

"It feels incredibly relevant right now, and specifically right now, because pornography that includes strangulation has just been outlawed in the UK."

Earlier this month, the government made it illegal for anyone to possess or publish porn that shows strangulation or suffocation.

That decision followed a review last year that found choking was "rife" on porn sites and had become normalised, particularly among younger people.

Coughlan and Cole say they were keen to make everything about their characters and the setting as relatable as possible to emphasise the shocking fallout.

"We needed one inciting incident that felt like something that could really plausibly happen between a couple, that it just goes slightly too far without consent, and it just blows everything up," Coughlan says.

"It's really important we see Steve's perspective in it because it makes him a normal guy.

"He's not this evil guy who's attacking Helen. He does bad things, but he's complicated. And hopefully you see them both as real people."

Filming the series without a script meant the actors were fully immersed in their characters, making them real not just for viewers but for themselves too.

"I'm not playing myself, but there's far less, let's say 'character' here than anything else I've ever done because a lot of this is about just reacting," Coughlan says.

She and Cole would film long takes, some lasting about an hour and often with heated exchanges, which might need to be shot multiple times.

Coughlan describes I Am Helen as "the most challenging thing in terms of material that I've ever worked on", adding for the first time in a role she needed counselling.

"You literally would be physically and mentally quite exhausted," she says.

"There were times that I said to Dominic [Savage] if he wanted to do a third take for example - and I've never said this before on set - but I actually don't think I have that in me because you hit a wall.

"When you're given that freedom, things happen and I think you can get some really interesting and also quite shocking stuff," he says.

For him, that came when he damaged a fridge on set with a punch.

But it's that authenticity of emotion which, while difficult for the actors, is what Coughlan thinks makes the series so engaging.

"When people watch the 'I Ams', they feel quite truthful," she says.

"I think that's a big reason as to why, to be honest."

Cole researched the manosphere online while developing his role and says he could see how people like Steve "quickly become lost in this quite simple ideology".

"The more interesting thing was the lower level, the kind of 'bro influencer' type people, who a lot of what they say is actually quite good," he says.

"You know, 'go to the gym, be healthy, look your best'.

"But occasionally they veer into comments on male and female societal roles and how a woman should stay at home."

For someone like Steve, who Cole says wants a traditional relationship and a family, those ideas left him "completely lost".

The characters quickly "get caught in a cycle", he says, as they find it harder and harder to understand each other.

"It starts off as a question, which becomes a debate, which becomes an argument, which becomes a huge bust-up, which becomes forgiveness, an apology, tears."

Coughlan says viewers have told her they expected the series to end with serious violence, perhaps even with Steve killing Helen.

But she was determined to avoid a shock factor so the characters didn't tip into being unrelatable.

"There's some very extreme moments in this, but some of them are not extreme," she says.

"It's better that he didn't [kill Helen] because as a viewer, you don't want people to go, 'well, if he does X, then that's the moment to leave'.

"From my perspective, you watch it and you go, 'you don't need to hit a threshold'.

"If you feel scared and uncomfortable, that's enough reason to get out of a situation."

If you have been affected by the issues raised in this article, help and support is available via BBC Action Line .

articles.title: How a teen gamer and his mother helped rescue a missing girl
articles.summary: When 16-year-old Landon Tresp met a teenage girl in an online game, it led to him and his mother helping the FBI rescue her from kidnapping.
articles.body:
Sixteen-year-old Landon Tresp was in the bedroom of his family's Colorado mountain home, playing an online game after finishing his daily chores, when he began chatting on his laptop with another player.

She was also a teenager, and the pair "kind of just clicked," he tells the BBC.

He told her he liked her name, and she confessed that it was an alias. She was a runaway, she said - and was being held against her will, hundreds of miles from home, though she didn't know exactly where. The girl, 17, and had been missing for more than a year.

Stunned, Landon felt "helpless," he says - and, after learning more details over two weeks of chatting, he decided to tell his mother, Khristina on 31 October this year. The 41-year-old nurse and mother of five was putting Halloween makeup on her younger children for trick-or-treating when he briefed her.

That set the mother and son on a path to track down his friend, contact her mother, cooperate with the FBI - and ultimately witness the rescue of the teen - only 24 hours after Landon first alerted Khristina to her plight.

"She had one opportunity to reach out her hand and ask for help, and she chose me," Khristina says of the girl, who was 15 when she went missing.

The Tresps have shared with BBC screenshots of communication with the girl and a photo matching the criminal complaint to corroborate their story.

Landon first told his mother about "Jenny" - whose identity the BBC is protecting - in mid-October, a few weeks before the rescue.

"He had mentioned something about maybe a week or so into talking to her that he met a girl online, and she was really sweet," says Khristina - who cautioned him that "you don't always know who's on the other side of the screen".

"She's just having a really hard time and looking for a friend," he told her.

But Landon was becoming increasingly concerned as Jenny told him more about her situation.

They'd met playing Among Us, a game Landon describes as "kind of like online space Clue".

After telling Landon that she was a runaway, "Jenny" said an older man had taken her across state lines and wouldn't let her leave. She was the subject of a missing person investigation, and she sent Landon links to stories about her disappearance. But she believed police were no longer looking for her.

Jenny was scared and desperate, and that's why Landon went to his mother.

Her maternal instincts on high alert, Khristina contacted Jenny herself on Discord, the encrypted platform.

During the conversation, Khristina said she told the Colorado mother how she'd been through "years of abuse in her life and lots and lots of problems".

Within hours, Jenny started calling Khristina "mama".

The Colorado mother knew things were serious when she read the missing persons articles. Jenny knew she was in Oregon and gave the name of a city, but she didn't know where she was being held exactly. Khristina knew she needed more. She told Jenny to find a piece of mail or another document in the house that had a full name on it, which the girl did.

"That's when I went to work," Khristina says, delving into tax and property records.

Khristina narrowed down addresses, then searched them on a real estate site to find pictures. She showed the photos to Jenny, who confirmed that the second one was where she was being held.

The "next thing she asked me was to please not tell anyone until [her captor] was gone - that he did have weapons in the house and she was very scared," Khristina said.

Jenny promised Khristina she'd call her back through the game platform when he left the next morning, and in the meantime Khristina began looking for the law enforcement agency that had been assigned to the missing teen's case. She contacted Jenny's mother on social media, spoke briefly to her on the phone and then got a call from an FBI agent.

"Have you seen her alive?'" the agent asked Khristina.

"And I said: 'I have; I video chatted with her, I've seen her, and she goes 'Oh my God, I cannot believe any of this'," Khristina recalled.

When Jenny called Khristina back after her alleged captor left home, the FBI monitored their conversation. According to the criminal complaint's record of the conversation, Jenny explained how she'd met Adam Hunter Harmel on social media in May 2025.

He'd told her he was disabled and his hips were "messed up," offering Jenny money if she'd help get him to Oregon.

After he picked her up in Utah, however, Harmel threw her phone into a river, drove her to Oregon and kept her in the basement. He forced her to sleep against the wall in his bed, with a knife under his pillow, to prevent her from escaping. He gave Jenny a cell phone with no ability to make calls, but it could connect to wifi, which is how she played the online game.

The 39-year-old "would become violent and aggressive", the document says, which included hitting her and sexually assaulting her.

He also allegedly forced Jenny to remove her braces with pliers so she wouldn't be identifiable.

As Khristina and the FBI heard all of this, law enforcement were staging to bring Jenny to safety, after being alerted to her whereabouts.

While Harmel was out of the home, officers were sent to the street and the address, and Khristina was prepping Jenny for her run to freedom.

She'd unsuccessfully tried escaping before, she told Khristina.

Law enforcement was "phenomenal…giving me an update, you know, 'We're nine minutes out, we're seven minutes out,'" says Khristina, who was on the phone with Jenny the entire time, her son Landon watching at her side.

Khristina could hear other people in the home with Jenny, and she was afraid that someone would catch wind of what was happening and harm the girl.

But she kept any of those fears from Jenny.

"I want you to take three deep breaths with me," she told the teen. "When an officer tells me to go, and I relay that message to you, I want you to run up those stairs as fast as you can … Grab that basement door.

"I want you to keep going down that hallway and grab that front door… do not stop.'"

The mother and son watched breathlessly as Jenny ran into the arms of a state trooper.

Harmel is now in federal custody and has been charged in a criminal complaint with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity. Local Oregon media also reported he'd been accused of sexually abusing a six-year-old in the months before Jenny disappeared - and a sexual abuse protective order was granted against him in March 2025.

A lawyer for the defendant did not respond to a BBC request for comment.

Jenny, meanwhile, remains in daily communication with Khristina and Landon - who still enjoys playing online games with her.

"Sometimes we just sit on video chat, just so she knows she has someone that cares," Khristina says. "She was on video last night when I cooked dinner …it's nice to know that when she has a bad day or a bad moment, she can call me right away or call Landon right away."

"She's doing great for what she's gone through."

They haven't met in person yet, but they're in the process of trying to make that happen.

"I hope I can put my arms around her soon," Khristina says.

articles.title: Paolo Bulgari, Italian jeweler who turned his family’s business into a global luxury brand, dies at 89
articles.summary: ATHENS, Greece — Paolo Bulgari, the grandson of a Greek silversmith who helped transform the family jewelry business into a global luxury brand synonymous with Italian glamour and design, has died.
articles.body: ATHENS, Greece — Paolo Bulgari, the grandson of a Greek silversmith who helped transform the family jewelry business into a global luxury brand synonymous with Italian glamour and design, has died. He was 89. His family announced his death Saturday, describing him as “the greatest jeweler of our time” and praising his humanity and entrepreneurial talent. Bulgari presided for decades over a brand celebrated by supermodels, Hollywood stars and collectors for its bold designs and distinctive use of color. Born in Rome in 1937, he was the grandson of Sotirios Voulgaris, who founded the jewelry business after leaving Greece. Originally from Paramythia, a mountain village in the Epirus region of northwestern Greece renowned for its silver jewelry, Voulgaris fled Ottoman rule and settled in Naples before opening a shop in Rome, adapting both his craft and his family name to his new home. Paolo Bulgari joined the family business shortly after leaving school. Working alongside his father, Giorgio, he initially focused on precious stones, developing an expertise in gemstones that would inform his work as a designer and businessman throughout his career. Turning away from the delicate aesthetic associated with Parisian jewelry houses, the Bulgari family embraced bold gemstones, rich yellow gold, generous proportions and unexpected combinations of color. Drawing inspiration from ancient Rome and Italy’s artistic heritage, the distinctive style helped set the brand apart internationally. Alongside his brother Nicola and nephew Francesco Trapani, Bulgari led the company’s expansion into major luxury markets, opening stores in New York, Paris, Geneva and Monte Carlo. The business diversified beyond jewelry into watches, perfumes, leather goods and, eventually, hotels. Heading the group since the mid-1980s, Bulgari guided the company through a period of significant international growth. Its jewelry was a fixture on celebrities spanning from Elizabeth Taylor to Zendaya. Tall and silver-haired, he occasionally appeared alongside the stars wearing his creations, maintaining a characteristically reserved presence. In 2011, the family sold a controlling stake in the company to French luxury conglomerate LVMH in a deal valued at more than $5 billion, ending decades of direct family control. Despite his association with the glamorous world of international luxury, Bulgari frequently referred to his family’s humble start. In 2019, he and his wife established the Paolo Bulgari Foundation to support young people through schooling and job training in disadvantaged neighborhoods on the outskirts of Rome. “Many people don’t know it,” he wrote in the foundation’s introduction, “but at the origin of my surname there is a story of migration.” His funeral will be held Monday at the Basilica of Santa Croce in Rome.

articles.title: An Arizona father signed a deed to his son in 2015 but used the wrong street address, then signed another deed for the property in 2019; an appeals court has upheld the son's earlier claim and voided later deeds
articles.summary: A minor slip in a property deed can catalyze a long legal battle, particularly if claims are made years later.
articles.body: A minor slip in a property deed can catalyze a long legal battle, particularly if claims are made years later. In Arizona, a dispute arose over a property transfer document executed by a father to his son in 2015 because the street address listed on the document was incorrect. In 2019, the father transferred the same Phoenix property to a business entity, and the competing ownership claims eventually reached the Arizona Court of Appeals, which upheld the son’s earlier claim and affirmed the invalidation of the later deeds.A disputed property transfer in 2015In 2015, Robert Olsen claimed ownership of a property in Phoenix through a quitclaim deed signed by his father, the Arizona Court of Appeals said. Although the deed mistakenly gave a common address in Seligman, Arizona, it correctly described the Phoenix property by its legal description.The document was recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder’s Office, giving public notice of the transfer. The court noted that a properly executed and recorded quitclaim deed is presumed valid if the grantor signed it and delivered it to the recipient.The difference between the street address and legal description later became a point of contention in the ownership dispute.Second transfer brings forth competing claimsIn 2019 Olsen’s father conveyed the Phoenix property by warranty deed to Bonitas Casitas LLC, the Arizona Court of Appeals explained. Later, the company claimed ownership of the asset, despite it having been transferred to Olsen.The dispute escalated when Olsen executed a special warranty deed conveying the property to the Robert Olsen Property Trust. A deed of trust was also filed against the property.In 2020, Bonitas sued Olsen alleging he had wrongfully recorded documents concerning property. Olsen and the trust filed counterclaims, claiming Bonitas and its business associate, Gregory Best, recorded the 2019 warranty deed and a 2020 correction deed improperly.Bonitas filed a deed of correction, which purported to change the legal description in Olsen’s 2015 deed from the Phoenix property to the Seligman property.Court rules earlier deed remained in effectThe Arizona Court of Appeals focused on whether Bonitas had established a legal ownership interest when the disputed documents were recorded.The court noted that Bonitas failed to successfully challenge the validity of Olsen's 2015 quitclaim deed. It also found the company didn’t establish ownership through a formal quiet title action, the proper legal way to adjudicate conflicting claims to real estate.The court also observed that public records, including the title history maintained by the county recorder and records maintained by the Maricopa County Assessor, recognized Olsen’s prior ownership claim.Therefore, Olsen and the trust retained title when the later deeds were recorded.Appeals court affirms voidance of later deedsOn November 19, 2026, the Arizona Court of Appeals affirmed the superior court’s decision invalidating Bonitas’ 2019 warranty deed and Best’s 2020 correction deed. It also upheld the order to remove both documents from records with the Maricopa County Recorder.The appeals court also approved the substitution of Tamarindo Investments LLC, which purchased the property from the trust in 2023, as the successor party in the litigation.The Court awarded Tamarindo reasonable attorney fees and costs, subject to appellate rules.Image Courtesy: Google GeminiYou use AI every day. articles.title: Ballistic missile attack on Zelenskyy’s hometown in central Ukraine kills 2 and wounds dozens
articles.summary: KYIV, Ukraine — A Russian strike on the center of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s hometown, Kryvyi Rih, killed two people and wounded 60 others, local officials said Saturday.
articles.body: KYIV, Ukraine — A Russian strike on the center of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s hometown, Kryvyi Rih, killed two people and wounded 60 others, local officials said Saturday. Meanwhile, a Russian cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad caught fire in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday after it was hit by drones, Finnish and Russian officials said. It was not clear who struck the ship not far from the Russian border. The Finnish prime minister warned that the war was spilling into the region. A 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman were killed in the attack Friday night on Kryvyi Rih in central Ukraine, Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of the city administration, wrote on Telegram. Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the regional military administration, said 60 people were wounded, including six children. The strike caused four fires and damaged about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and an industrial facility, as well as businesses and vehicles, Vilkul said. Video footage published by the regional branch of the Ukrainian State Emergency Service appeared to show further strikes while ambulance and firefighting crews were responding at the scene, as fires burned around them. “First, two ballistic missiles. And then, when the emergency and rescue operation began, three more rockets hit doctors, rescuers and utility workers,” Vilkul wrote on Telegram. The attack added to uncertainty about the prospects for ongoing talks brokered by Washington. It also came hours after two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland, in what its prime minister said was likely a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country. In the unprecedented two-week military exercise that began Nov. 9 in southeastern Poland, forces are preparing for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine aimed at helping to stabilize the country and rebuild its military. European countries previously have expressed alarm at what they deem to be Russia’s attempts to destabilize the continent. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte, speaking to reporters in Warsaw on Saturday, called the airspace violation “dangerous” and said all allies stood “in full solidarity with Poland.” “NATO will defend every inch of Polish territory,” Rutte said. He said the alliance functioned “as it should” on Friday morning, when NATO jets supported Polish F-16s scrambled as Russian objects approached Polish airspace. NATO’s top military commander was assessing the alliance’s defenses and would make adjustments if needed, Rutte said. Crimean Bridge strikes ‘fair response,’ Zelenskyy says At a meeting with U.K. Defense Secretary Wes Streeting in Kyiv, Zelenskyy said Saturday that Ukraine’s repeated attacks on the Kerch Bridge linking occupied Crimea with the Russian mainland were a “fair response” to scores of Russian attacks on Ukrainian bridges. He said that Russia President Vladimir Putin had “attacked Ukrainian bridges 109 times.” “Not the number of missiles — the number of attacks,” he said. “This is important, that’s why it’s our absolutely fair response.” The Ukrainian leader said Putin “doesn’t want to stop the war” and is looking to escalate. He also rejected Putin’s claim that the Kerch bridge is used exclusively by civilian traffic. “If he can use internet, he can use it and see tanks, armored vehicles, artillery,” the Ukrainian leader said. Streeting called the airspace violations in Poland “an outrageous provocation” and urged allies to respond by stepping up support for Ukraine. “The more they try and deter Europe from supporting Ukraine, the more we will step up,” he said. Zelenskyy reacts to Trump calling Putin his friend The drone incursion in Poland stoked tensions between Europe and Moscow just as the U.S. tries to add momentum to talks it is mediating on ending the war that began with Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago. U.S. President Donald Trump discussed the war with Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at a summit in China on Thursday, according to his envoy Steve Witkoff. Trump called Putin his “friend” during the meeting and continued to tout their relationship at a White House news conference Friday. Asked about Trump’s remarks in an interview with CNN, Zelenskyy called Putin “a killer.” “For us, he is an enemy. And of course, for us, he is a killer,” Zelenskyy said Friday. He warned that describing the Russian leader in friendly terms could mean “he doesn’t feel enough pressure.” Russian cargo ship is on fire in the Gulf of Finland Two drones attacked the vessel in “neutral waters” 3 nautical miles from the Russian border, Alexander Drozdenko, the governor of Russia’s Leningrad region, wrote on Telegram. He later said the crew had not needed to be evacuated and that the situation on board was “under control,” with preparations being made for the vessel to resume navigation. The ship drifted into Finnish territorial waters, the Finnish Border Guard said in a statement, adding that it posed no danger to maritime traffic. Finnish border guards were carrying out a rescue operation and preparing for possible environmental damage, it said. According to a statement sent to Estonian media, Estonian authorities received a report that a fire had broken out on the Russian cargo ship Sparta II, which was sailing in the Gulf of Finland. The ship had drifted out of Estonia’s exclusive economic zone earlier Saturday. According to preliminary reports, explosions occurred on board. “War is spilling into our immediate vicinity,” Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo wrote on X. Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave on the Baltic Sea, between Poland and Lithuania. Finland’s Defense Ministry also said that a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating Finnish airspace around noon Saturday, flying about 2.5 miles into the country. Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen said the incident may have been related to rescue or monitoring operations involving the damaged ship. Elsewhere in Ukraine, 11 people, including two children, were wounded when a Russian drone attacked a five-story apartment building in the Kharkiv region, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said Saturday. One person was wounded in a Russian attack on the capital, Kyiv, according to the service. In Russia, local officials said Saturday that Ukrainian drone attacks wounded three people in the Bryansk and Belgorod border regions.

articles.body: Iran has said reopening the Strait of Hormuz would not be difficult if the United States accepts reasonable conditions under international law, while warning that it would take all necessary measures to break Washington's economic blockade. The remarks came as US President Donald Trump reiterated that any agreement with Tehran must permanently prevent it from acquiring nuclear weapons.Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi on Saturday described the US-imposed blockade as a hostile act and warned of retaliation. articles.title: NYC suspect in Chinatown fatal beating had 5 open cases as Mamdani pushes plan to close Rikers
articles.summary: Alexander Florentino faced five open cases before the fatal Chinatown attack, arriving as Zohran Mamdani unveiled a plan to close Rikers Island by 2032.
articles.body: A 25-year-old homeless New York City man charged with beating a 62-year-old woman to death and assaulting a man in Manhattan's Chinatown was free despite five open criminal cases — including three arrests in November alone — just as Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled a plan to close the city's Rikers Island jail. NYPD officers arrested Alexander Florentino at 11:30 a.m. Saturday in the 5th Precinct on charges of murder, attempted murder, two counts of strangulation, burglary, assault and attempted assault. New York State Unified Court System records show Florentino was awaiting Dec. 14 court appearances across five pending Manhattan Criminal Court dockets, meaning he had been released ahead of Friday's fatal attack. ILLEGAL ALIEN ACCUSED OF ATTEMPTED MURDER AT LARGE AFTER RIKERS RELEASE DESPITE ICE DETAINER: DHS Most recently, police arrested Florentino on Nov. 18 in connection with an incident two days earlier, court records show. NYPD Transit Bureau officers also arrested him twice on Nov. 11 in separate cases tied to incidents on Nov. 11 and Aug. 3, and he had two open arrests from Sept. 2 and Sept. 28. The repeat arrests came just a day after Mamdani unveiled a six-year plan to shutter Rikers Island by 2032 by cutting the jail population from roughly 6,700 to 4,100 and expanding alternatives to detention. "Too many New Yorkers have experienced our criminal legal system as a revolving door, where they cycle in and out of jail because there is too little energy expended towards helping them rebuild their lives," Mamdani said Friday. "We have a legal and moral obligation to close Rikers." PENN STATION STABBING VICTIM SLAMS MAMDANI, DA BRAGG FOR SUSPECT BEING FREE ON STREETS Police said officers responded to 27 Catherine St. around 3: 22 p.m. Friday and found the 62-year-old woman unconscious and unresponsive with trauma to her face and neck. Emergency medical workers transported her to NYC Health + Hospitals/Bellevue, where she was pronounced dead. Officers also found a 66-year-old man with a laceration to the right side of his face after being struck over the head with a glass bottle, police said. He was taken to Bellevue in stable condition. Authorities have not released the woman's identity pending family notification, and the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner will determine her cause of death. Police have not disclosed a possible motive or said whether Florentino knew the victims. articles.title: Psychology says people who regularly change their profile pictures may be more conscious of how others perceive them; what your constantly changing display picture may say about self-image, social validation, and the need to belong online
articles.summary: Think about the last time you changed your WhatsApp or Instagram profile picture. Was it a new haircut? A trip? A good photo from a wedding?
articles.body: Think about the last time you changed your WhatsApp or Instagram profile picture. Was it a new haircut? A trip? A good photo from a wedding? Or did you just feel like changing the photo that day?Most of us might never even think about it, because it takes two taps and a few seconds.Many people let their profile pictures remain unchanged for months, but some change their DP on almost every occasion or when they put on a new look.But a profile picture is not like any other photo on your phone. It remains next to your name in chats, comments, and friend lists and is often the first thing a stranger or a new colleague clicks to identify you.Even without knowing it, every time we choose one, we are quietly answering a small question: how do I want to be seen?Let us see what psychology has to say about it.Why do some people keep their profile pictures for years, and others keep changing them every second day?A profile picture may not feel very significant, but researchers treat it as an important one. A 2017 study published in Frontiers in Psychology describes it as the main representation of the profile owner. It is also the first image potential new friends see before they send a request. So every update might come across as how we want to be seen.What does your DP say about your self-esteem and psychological benefit?One of the best-known studies was done by Cornell researchers, published in Cyberpsychology, Behavior, and Social Networking in 2011. According to Cornell's own report, 63 students sat in front of a Facebook page, a mirror, or a blank screen. Those who looked at their Facebook profiles reported more positive feelings about themselves than the other groups. Those who edited their profiles during the exercise reported the highest self-esteem.The reason, according to Hancock, is that Facebook lets people put their best face forward. They choose what to show and filter out what might look bad. He described the result as evidence of "a psychological benefit of Facebook."The need for belonging and why do reactions matter so much?Psychologists Roy Baumeister and Mark Leary argued in 1995, in Psychological Bulletin, that the need to belong is a "powerful, fundamental, and extremely pervasive motivation." We want regular, friendly contact with other people. According to EBSCO's research overview, this need is also associated with the need for approval from others. A new photo brings small social rewards, such as a comment, a reaction, or a message saying "looking good!" Each one ‘says’ that we still belong.So, changing your picture often is not a flaw; instead, it might just be a way of saying "this is who I am right now," and might just help you ask yourself once in a while why you are changing it. If the answer is "I like this photo," that is healthy. If it is "I need people to notice me," that is worth reconsidering.
